StepTime

Jira / Team ’26 Europe / Motion study

From Done to an endless wall.

How one card drop becomes a celebration, a 3D field, and a world of moving work.

One drawing. 12 moments. Scroll to follow the work.

Begin the story ↓

01 / 12 0.0s

The keynote board

Three chapters of work sit beside an empty Done column.

How it works

The board is the starting frame. Keep the work in view while one orange card becomes the subject. The study removes labels and cover art so the handoff is easier to follow.

View this moment ↗

02 / 12 1.2s

One card lands

A human cursor carries Agent Session Tracking into Done, then releases it.

How it works

The cursor stays attached to the same point on the card through its lift, travel and release. Once it lands, the full face fits inside the Done column’s clip window.

View this moment ↗

03 / 12 2.4s

A local reward

A small puff opens around the landed card, then clears.

How it works

A landing rectangle seeds a small burst around the new arrival. This local reward clears before the next act. In production, it uses the shared WebGL confetti renderer and its own landing wait.

View this moment ↗

04 / 12 3.5s

The whole deck completes

The cursor drags the rest of the selected work into Done as one stack. All 23 stories are complete and Done fills to its edge.

How it works

The readiness check tracks the required keynote cards. When that set is complete, the finale begins. In the study, every completed card moves with the cursor as one selection, and Done fills to the column’s edge.

View this moment ↗

05 / 12 4.7s

The celebration grows

A broad confetti burst changes the scale of the reward.

How it works

Two cannons fire upward and inward from opposite sides. Different depths, spins and speeds make the paper feel like a volume. The production player is prewarmed and can render through an OffscreenCanvas worker.

View this moment ↗

06 / 12 5.9s

Particles find an orbit

The burst gathers into a rotating funnel above Done.

How it works

The broad burst gathers into a rotating sink near Done. This celebration has its own show clock; the production finale clock begins when gathering finishes.

View this moment ↗

07 / 12 7.6s

Completion light

A light traces the three card borders, then a directional gradient passes across their faces.

How it works

Three light paths trace the actual card borders, followed by a directional gradient clipped to their faces. This is the refined study treatment. The linked production pass instead samples an image of the column through a fragment shader.

View this moment ↗

08 / 12 9.4s

The cards become a field

The deck separates into individually tilted paper cards; the camera recoils.

How it works

The production app captures the card faces as textures on thin Three.js sheets. Seeded positions, rotations and depth spread them into a field. Its sheet shader adds paper flutter and bending; the study uses solid SVG faces.

View this moment ↗

09 / 12 11.2s

Find the hero card

The camera crosses the field and closes on Agent Session Tracking.

How it works

The camera recoils, opens the field, then closes on Agent Session Tracking. Camera framing has its own authored path, separate from each card’s pose, so the subject remains clear as the space changes.

View this moment ↗

10 / 12 12.9s

Six features assemble

Six product faces land around Team ’26 in the keynote bento.

How it works

The hero lands first, then five other sheets assemble around it. In production, each animated sheet hands off to its matching HTML tile after touchdown. The shared pose makes that change read as one object.

View this moment ↗

11 / 12 14.7s

Throw into a larger world

The main cursor carries the title into its moving wall gap while the six tiles tumble outward.

How it works

The six tiles travel toward moving gaps in a larger wall. A staged cursor carries the title into its own slot. The cards keep their mixed proportions through the journey rather than becoming uniform tiles.

View this moment ↗

12 / 12 20.0s

A wall that people keep moving

Teammates reach in from the leading edge, grip incoming work, lower it into separate slots, and let go as the wall glides.

How it works

A packed wall of wide, tall, square and small cards, seen straight on, scrolls sideways. New columns enter from the right as old ones leave, with no duplicate rows. Teammate cursors keep placing work; Play lets this final state continue until paused.
